text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $x\log _{e}x\frac{dy}{dx}+y=x^{2}\log _{e}x,(x>1)$. If $y(2)=2$, then $y(e)$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x\ln x\frac{dy}{dx}+y=x^{2}\ln x$

$\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{1}{x\ln x}.y=x$

I.F. $=e^{\int \frac{1}{x\ln x}dx}=e^{\int \frac{1}{t}dt}$, where $t=\ln x$

$=e^{\ln t}=t=\ln x$

$y.\ln x=\int x\ln x=\frac{x^{2}}{2}\ln x-\int \frac{x^{2}}{2}.\frac{1}{x}$

$y\ln x=\frac{x^{2}}{2}\ln x-\frac{x^{2}}{4}+C$ ..... (i)

$y(2)=2\Rightarrow C=1$

Putting $x=e$ in (i),

$y=\frac{e^{2}}{4}+1=\frac{4+e^{2}}{4}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: Let R be a relation defined on $\mathrm{ℕ}$ as $a\mathrm{R}b$ if $2a+3b$ is a multiple of $5,a,b\in \mathrm{ℕ}$. Then R is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
a R b if 2a + 3b = 5m, m $\in$ $l$

(1) $(a,a)\in R$ as $2a+3a=5a,a\in N$

Hence, R is reflexive

(2) If $(a,b)\in R$ then $2a+3b=5m$

Now, $5(a+b)=5n$

$3a+2b+2a+3b=5n$

$\therefore$ $3a+2b=5(n-m)$

$\therefore$ $(b,a)\in R$

$\therefore$ R is symmetric

(3) If $(a,b)\in R$ and $(b,c)\in R$ then

$2a+3b=5m,2b+3c=5n$

$\Rightarrow 2a+5b+3c=5(m+n)$

$\Rightarrow 2a+3c=5(m+n-b)$

$\therefore$ $(a,c)\in R$

$\therefore$ R is transitive

Hence, R is equivalence relation.

Option (1) is correct.

text: If $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\widehat{k},\vec{b}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\widehat{k},\vec{c}=7\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+4\widehat{k},\vec{r}\times \vec{b}+\vec{b}\times \vec{c}=\vec{0}$ and $\vec{r}\quad .\vec{a}=0$. Then $\vec{r}\quad .\vec{c}$ is equal to :

solution.body:
$(\vec{r}-\vec{c})\times \vec{b}=0$

$\vec{r}=λ\vec{b}+\vec{c}$

$\Rightarrow λ\vec{b}.\vec{a}+\vec{c}.\vec{a}=0$

$\Rightarrow λ(3)+(7+8)=0$

$\Rightarrow λ=-5$

$\vec{r}=-5\vec{b}+\vec{c}$

$=-5\hat{i}-5\hat{j}-5\widehat{k}+(7\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+4\widehat{k})$

$=2\hat{i}-8\hat{j}-\widehat{k}$

$\therefore$ $\vec{r}\quad .\vec{c}=14+24-4=34$

text: The number of 3 digit numbers, that are divisible by either 3 or 4 but not divisible by 48, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Three-digit multiples of 3: $⌊\dfrac{999}{3}⌋-⌊\dfrac{99}{3}⌋=333-33=300$.

Three-digit multiples of 4: $⌊\dfrac{999}{4}⌋-⌊\dfrac{99}{4}⌋=249-24=225$.

Numbers divisible by both 3 and 4 are the multiples of 12: $⌊\dfrac{999}{12}⌋-⌊\dfrac{99}{12}⌋=83-8=75$.

By inclusion-exclusion, the three-digit numbers divisible by 3 or 4 number $300+225-75=450$.

Every multiple of 48 is a multiple of 3, so all of them are among these 450 numbers. Three-digit multiples of 48 run from $48\times 3=144$ to $48\times 20=960$, which is $20-2=18$ numbers.

Required count $=450-18=432$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: The set of all values of $λ$ for which the equation $\cos ^{2}2x-2\sin ^{4}x-2\cos ^{2}x=λ$ has a real solution $x$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $c=\cos ^{2}x$, so $c$ takes every value in $[0,1]$. Then $\cos 2x=2c-1$ and $\sin ^{2}x=1-c$, so

$λ=(2c-1)^{2}-2(1-c)^{2}-2c$

$=4c^{2}-4c+1-2+4c-2c^{2}-2c=2c^{2}-2c-1=2\left (c-\dfrac{1}{2}\right )^{2}-\dfrac{3}{2}$

On $[0,1]$ the least value is at $c=\dfrac{1}{2}$, giving $λ=-\dfrac{3}{2}$, and the greatest is at $c=0$ or $c=1$, giving $λ=2\cdot \dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{3}{2}=-1$.

Being continuous in $c$, $λ$ takes every value between these, so the equation has a real solution exactly for $λ\in \left [-\dfrac{3}{2},-1\right ]$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: The area of the region $A=\left \{(x,y):|\cos x-\sin x|\leq y\leq \sin x,0\leq x\leq \frac{π}{2}\right \}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$|\cos x-\sin x|\leq y\leq \sin x$

Intersection point of $\cos x-\sin x=\sin x$

$\Rightarrow \tan x=\frac{1}{2}$

Let $ψ=\tan ^{-1}\frac{1}{2}$

So, $\tan ψ=\frac{1}{2},\sin ψ=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}},\cos ψ=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$


[IMG]


Area $=\int\limits _{\tan ^{-1}\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{π}{4}}(\sin x-(\cos x-\sin x))dx+\int\limits _{\frac{π}{4}}^{\frac{π}{2}}(\sin x-(\sin x-\cos x))dx$

$=\int\limits _{\tan ^{-1}\frac{1}{2}}^{π/4}(2\sin x-\cos x)dx+\int\limits _{π/4}^{π/2}\cos xdx$

$=[-2\cos x-\sin x]_{\tan ^{-1}\frac{1}{2}}^{π/4}+[\sin x]_{π/4}^{π/2}$

$=-\sqrt{2}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+2\cos (\tan ^{-1}\frac{1}{2})+\sin (\tan ^{-1}\frac{1}{2})+\left (1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )$

$=-\sqrt{2}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+2\left (\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right )+\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right )+1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$=\sqrt{5}-2\sqrt{2}+1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: Let $\vec{a}=4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}$ and $\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+5\widehat{k}$. If $\vec{c}$ is a vector such that $\vec{c}.\left (\vec{a}\times \vec{b}\right )+25=0,\vec{c}.(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\widehat{k})=4$, and projection of $\vec{c}$ on $\vec{a}$ is 1, then the projection of $\vec{c}$ on $\vec{b}$ equals :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[\begin{array}{lll} \vec{c} & \vec{a} & \vec{b} \end{array}]=-25$

Let $\vec{c}=l\hat{i}+m\hat{j}+n\widehat{k}$

$\left |\begin{array}{lll} l & m & n \\ 4 & 3 & 0 \\ 3 & -4 & 5 \end{array}\right |=-25$

$\Rightarrow 3l-4m-5n=-5$ ..... (i)

$\vec{c}.(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\widehat{k})=4$

$\Rightarrow l+m+n=4$ ..... (ii)

$\frac{\vec{c}.\vec{a}}{|\vec{a}|}=1\Rightarrow \vec{c}.\vec{a}=5$

$\Rightarrow 4l+3m=5$ ...... (iii)

Using (i), (ii) and (iii)

$l=2,m=-1,n=3$

Now, $\frac{\vec{c}.\vec{b}}{|\vec{b}|}=\frac{25}{5\sqrt{2}}=\frac{5}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\therefore$ Option (4) is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: The shortest distance between the lines $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+8}{-7}=\frac{z-4}{5}$ and $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y-2}{1}=\frac{z-6}{-3}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{r}_{1}=\hat{i}-8\hat{j}+4\widehat{k}$

$\vec{r}_{2}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+6\widehat{k}$

$\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-7\hat{j}+5\widehat{k}$

$\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\widehat{k}$

S.D. $=\frac{\left |\begin{array}{lll} \vec{r}_{1}-\vec{r}_{2} & \begin{array}{ll} \vec{a} & \vec{b} \end{array} \end{array}\right |}{\left |\vec{a}\times \vec{b}\right |}$

$\left [\begin{array}{lll} \vec{r}_{1}-\vec{r}_{2} & \begin{array}{ll} \vec{a} & \vec{b} \end{array} \end{array}\right ]=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 0 & -10 & -2 \\ 2 & -7 & 5 \\ 2 & 1 & -3 \end{array}\right |$

$\therefore$ $10(-16)-2(16)=-192$

$\left |\left [\begin{array}{lll} \vec{r}_{1}-\vec{r}_{2} & \begin{array}{ll} \vec{a} & \vec{b} \end{array} \end{array}\right ]\right |=192$

$\vec{a}\times \vec{b}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \widehat{k} \\ 2 & -7 & 5 \\ 2 & 1 & -3 \end{array}\right |=16\hat{i}+16\hat{j}+16\widehat{k}$

$\left |\vec{a}\times \vec{b}\right |=16\sqrt{3}$

S.D. $=\frac{192}{16\sqrt{3}}=4\sqrt{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: Let A be a symmetric matrix such that $|\mathrm{A}|=2$ and $\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 1 \\ 3 & \frac{3}{2} \end{array}\right ]A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 2 \\ α & β \end{array}\right ]$. If the sum of the diagonal elements of A is $s$, then $\frac{βs}{α^{2}}$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A=\left (\begin{array}{ll} a & c \\ c & b \end{array}\right )$

$|A|=ab-c^{2}=2$ ...... (1)

$\left (\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 1 \\ 3 & \frac{3}{2} \end{array}\right )\left (\begin{array}{ll} a & c \\ c & b \end{array}\right )=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 2 \\ α & β \end{array}\right )$

$2a+c=1$ ..... (2)

$2c+b=2$ ..... (3)

$3a+\frac{3}{2}c=α$ .... (4)

$3c+\frac{3}{2}b=β$ ..... (5)

From (1), (2) and (3)

$a=\frac{3}{4},b=3,c=-\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ Now $α=\frac{6}{4}$

$β=3$

$s=\frac{15}{4}$

$\frac{βs}{α^{2}}=\frac{3\times \frac{15}{4}}{\left (\frac{6}{4}\right )^{2}}=\frac{\frac{45}{4}}{\frac{9}{4}}=5$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift
